coverage_note: 10:00-13:48 Medi on a work phone call in English (customer, rugs) - no lesson content. 19:49-23:14 connection drop (gap). 41:46 Medi line is an aside to someone else. 04:02 engine wrote الجو شوك = شوب (he repeats شوب at 04:06). 06:36/06:40 an earlier engine pass wrote مشجع for his repeat of her متشجع (pronunciation, not scored). Echo candidates checked: none is a sound-alike of Arabic (Maybe., Um, Uh-huh, The week's beginning = real English). Long English rule-discussion stretches 47:18-1:04:54 (awal / oola / taani / nafs / 8eir), with Latin-letter Arabic from Medi (awal tamreen, laffe, nafs ishi). No laazem_noun fix voiced (04:14 she only asked laazem ish?).

rows.amal_said: عندنا.
rows.why: He meant his shop has customers (we), said 3indhum (they); Amal recast عندنا and he repeated it at 00:34.

rows.amal_said: شو يعني لسه الزباين يروحوا؟ ... لا، لا الزباين يروحوا.
rows.why: He used lissa (still/not yet) for 'until'; Amal asked what he meant and gave la (until): 'the one we know is لا'.

rows.amal_said: واحد.
rows.chat: yoam el-5amees, wa7ad 3ashara alafain u sitte u 3eshreen
rows.why: For the date (the 1st) he started with the feminine wa7de; Amal recast واحد and he later states 'dates are واحد, times are واحدة'.

rows.amal_said: واحد. ... هيك الساعة واحدة.
rows.why: Clock time takes the feminine number; Amal echoed his واحد as a question, he fixed to واحدة and she confirmed الساعة واحدة.

rows.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة، uh، أخ- أخ- أخضر
rows.amal_said: بلوزة شو؟
rows.chat: el-yoam balbes bluze 5adra u bantaloan beige u kundara binniyye
rows.why: Masculine adjective on feminine بلوزة; Amal prompted 'بلوزة شو؟' and he fixed to خضرا ('it's feminine').
rows.english: Today I'm wearing a green blouse.

rows.amal_said: لازم إيش؟ ... آآآه. Air conditioning باهد.
rows.right: بحتاج air conditioning / لازم + verb (my reading)
rows.why: laazem goes straight onto a thing with no verb (GR-27); Amal only asked 'laazem ish?' and never supplied a verb, so it is let-pass.

rows.amal_said: Hafiz is a motivation، بس what's about motivated؟ ... متشـ... متشجع.
rows.why: Asked for yesterday's word 'motivated' he said 7aafez (motivation, a different word); Amal said that is motivation and supplied متشجع (sheet: motivated | Mitshajje3 | متشجع).

rows.medi_said: Is it-- Is there a verb for حساب? you guys use it?
rows.amal_said: بحسب.
rows.why: He asked for the verb 'to consider' and Amal supplied بحسب - a didn't-know.

rows.amal_said: هاي، هاي، برا، برا. برا.
rows.right: متشجع للدرس (my reading; she used متشجع للـ شغل / متشجع إله)
rows.why: mitshajje3 takes la- (Amal's own questions: متشجع للـ شغل, متشجع لـ العربي, متشجع إله); he dropped it and she said bravo.

rows.medi_said: أنا فـ، أنا فـ، أنا في الـ Wi-Fi? Is that how you say it?
rows.amal_said: Yeah I'm on the wifi أنا عالـ wifi. ... على الـ، عالـ.
rows.why: He used fi (in) for 'on the Wi-Fi'; Amal recast أنا عالـ wifi and he repeated أنا على الـ.

rows.medi_said: So شنطتي ... Would it be الشغل؟
rows.amal_said: Yes, but what's work bag without any my or yours?
rows.why: He put the owner ending on the first noun (shanteti + el-shu8ul); Amal prompted on 'work bag' alone and he fixed to 'Shantet Shogoli, not Shanteti Shogoli'.

rows.amal_said: That would mean is red. ... the adjective after it should be definitive as well.
rows.why: Adjective after a definite (possessed) noun needs el-; without it the phrase becomes a sentence 'is red', as Amal said.

rows.medi_said: So would it be شنتت، شنتت شغلي الأحمر، الأحمر،
rows.amal_said: الحمرا.
rows.why: شنتة is feminine; Amal recast الحمرا and he repeated it, noting he got it wrong here.

rows.amal_said: ما فيهن means there aren't here or there isn't here. ... Yeah, مشون.
rows.why: For 'is not here' he used ma fi (there isn't); Amal explained the meaning, he tried مش هون and she confirmed.
rows.english: My red work bag is not here.

rows.amal_said: ليش؟ لا، ليش. ... It's just اسم. Why would it be feminine?
rows.why: He added the feminine idafa -t to esem (masculine); Amal said no, it is just اسم.

rows.amal_said: لا.
rows.why: First word of an idafa never takes el-; Amal said لا and he concluded 'So it's not الـ اسم'.
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.medi_said: So الـ اسم قديم. No, it's like اسم القديمة. Okay, I don't know.
rows.amal_said: لا. لا. You just change the gender of Adeem.
rows.why: For 'the old name of his school' the adjective goes at the end and takes the gender of the noun it describes (el-2adeem for esem); Amal said no and gave the gender rule.
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.amal_said: But her. Her favorite store. Her store favorite.
rows.chat: ma7al awa3iha el-mufaddal / ma7al el-awa3i el-mufadal 3indha
rows.why: 'her' was left out - the owner ending must go on the last noun; Amal prompted 'But her' and he said محل أواعيها المفضل at 36:38.

rows.amal_said: No. Even though in English we don't-- we say the, in Arabic we don't.
rows.why: Superlative a7san takes no el- on the noun; Amal said No and he fixed to أحسن محل.

rows.amal_said: Mm, it works, yeah. هذا أحسن محل is like more efficient
rows.why: محل is masculine so it is hada, not hadi; Amal said 'it works' and only re-phrased with هذا, never naming the gender.

rows.medi_said: Okay. So أحسن زبون ما، ما ما بتشتري إشي.
rows.amal_said: It's ما بي، ما بيشتري because it's زبون.
rows.right: أسوأ (my reading; her chat aswa2 zboon)
rows.why: The sentence was 'the worst customer is the one who doesn't buy' and he said a7san (best) for aswa2 (worse, on her sheet); she fixed only the verb.
rows.english: The worst customer doesn't buy anything.

rows.medi_said: ما ما بتشتري إشي. ما بتشتري. ما بتشتري.
rows.amal_said: It's ما بي، ما بيشتري because it's زبون.
rows.why: Verb must be he-form for زبون; Amal recast ما بيشتري and he repeated it.
rows.english: The worst customer doesn't buy anything.

rows.amal_said: بحبه.
rows.why: The verb needs the pointer ending back to 7ada; Amal recast بحبه and he said 'Oh, I do. There's a pointer.'
rows.english: the person I like the most

rows.amal_said: Why? ... بس if you say the week's beginning, now you'd have to be إضافة ... It would be the first week.
rows.why: Asked what her الأسبوع الأول means he said 'the week's beginning'; Amal challenged it and he reached 'the first week' (awal after the noun = adjective).

rows.medi_said: Il awal il tamreen or il tamreen il awal is the first exercise.
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. ... Of course.
rows.why: awal before the noun never takes el- (Amal at 47:59 and on her sheet); 'il awal il tamreen' passed with Mm-hmm.

rows.amal_said: Al oola. ... Al laffa al oola.
rows.chat: awal laffe, awal el-lafe, el-laffe el-oola
rows.why: Repeating her phrase he dropped el- on the adjective (and later لفّة الأولى dropped it on the noun); Amal recast al laffa al oola several times.

rows.amal_said: Nafs al ishi. ... نفس الـ إشي the same thing. نفس إشي doesn't mean anything.
rows.why: nafs needs el- on the noun; Amal recast Nafs al ishi and said نفس إشي means nothing.

rows.amal_said: بشوفك. Bye.
rows.why: Plain present 'see you' takes b- (Amal said بشوفك just before); his reply lacks it, possibly the engine dropping the b-.
